subject: butterfly
review_scope: Independent visual comparison of source-keys.png, design.png, revisions/keys-v1.png and source.json only. Four chronological still keys in 2x2 order; no normal-speed playback inspected and no motion approval.

timed_key_evidence.evidence: Source shows the butterfly perched on fingertips with its visible wing plane rising steeply above the fingers. Drawing keeps foot-to-finger contact but shows a broad wing projecting almost horizontally left, setting up a much more open wing pose.

Source remains perched with a similarly steep wing attitude. Drawing adds a prominently raised narrow wing while retaining the broad horizontal wing, increasing the opening change beyond the source still pair.
Source still has an upright wing with a small view/angle change. Drawing keeps the butterfly supported but further elevates the tall wing relative to the broad left lobe.

Source’s wing is upright and the finger composition shifts. Drawing ends with a tall closed-looking wing and the head/antennae on the left, producing a large open-to-upright pose change across the four keys rather than the source’s subtle perched variation.

main_gap: The perched contact survives, but the sequence invents a substantial wing-opening/closing progression. The source keys support subtle wing-angle changes while continuously perched. The selected design’s antenna loops and angular lobes remain visible but cannot justify changing the action.
bounded_repair: Replace only the butterfly wing poses across the four keys with consistently steep, near-closed wing planes matching each source still, varying their angle subtly around the same attached thorax; retain the existing fingers, feet, angular line character and looped antennae.
protected_strengths: All four drawings retain contact with the fingertips; none clearly depicts takeoff.
The hand supplies a clear scale and support cue.
Loop-ended antennae and polygonal wing edges preserve recognizable elements of the chosen QuickDraw design.
